messages.author: c388c66f81aaadc0
messages.subject: question on starve_mode input
parts:
Dear Mike,

we are trying to simulate our lizard's DEB in NichmapR. The outputs are quite reasonable under some conditions, but more surprising in others: structural mass decreases during some period of the year (see the figure attached). It happens in summer, when temperatures are hot and leaves very little activity time to the lizard, with the result that the lizard has very little to eat. I therefore suspect that this creates conditions in which the flux of mobilized energy that goes to growth + maintenance (kappa*pc) becomes smaller than maintenance requirements (pM). When I checked your latest posts on internet, it looks like NichemapR should be able to control how allocation changes in these conditions through the parameter starve_mode of the ectotherm function, which by default should be set to 1, although our output looks like it is set to 0. In any circumstance, in the version I'm using, which I believe to be the latest version available (v.3.2.1, from 10/12/2022, or maybe I'm missing something?), it seems like this starve_mode thing hasn't been implemented yet.

So is there any way to control starvation mode in v.3.2.1? or is there a newer version around or one that you would be willing to share before release? Or, do I need to be patient and wait for the next update? Or maybe, it might just be that I'm doing something wrong?

Thanks in advance,

Romain Richard

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: question on starve_mode input
parts:
Dear Romain,

The 'starvemode' option is something I've recently added. By default it (starvemode = 1) it uses the reproduction buffer in preference to structure. If you set it to 0 it will go straight to using structure. If you set it to 2 it will use reproduction buffer before it uses reserves. You can try it out if you get the latest version on github (devtools::install_github('mrke/NicheMapR' - but you need gfortran compilers installed). I'll be writing up that modification as part of a paper I'm putting together on modelling snakes with DEB theory (with other changes to allow feeding in meals as well as laying eggs at maturity stages > 0).

All the best,
Mike
